source: https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/paloalto/latest/paloalto_ca/0-0-0-77458 (Ch. 18.13 Multiple Family Residential RM-20, RM-30, RM-40)
https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/paloalto/latest/paloalto_ca/0-0-0-78729 (Ch. 18.20 Office, Research, Manufacturing MOR, ROLM, RP, GM)
notes: Densities reflect the Palo Alto Municipal Code Title 18 (Zoning) as amended through Housing Element compliance ordinances (2022-2024).
The RM district numbers (20, 30, 40) correspond to the maximum dwelling units per acre allowed in each district.
On Housing Element Opportunity Sites (designated per Sec. 18.14.020), modified/higher densities may apply per Table 1 of that section.
Where the Comprehensive Plan Land Use Element density differs from the Zoning Ordinance, the Comprehensive Plan prevails.

Palo Alto does not use a single explicit 'minimum density' for most base zones; min_density values of null indicate no codified minimum. Where minimums exist (e.g., on Housing Opportunity Sites), they are noted.
Commercial and industrial zones generally prohibit standalone residential unless the site is a Housing Inventory Site or mixed-use is permitted.
The formerly named RM-15 district was renamed RM-20 (and density increased from 15 to 20 du/ac) as part of the 2022 Housing Element compliance amendments.

RE.description: Residential Estate district (Ch. 18.10). Low-density single-family residential with large lots (min ~20,000 sq ft). Intended for estate-style homes in areas with semi-rural character. Max approx 2 du/ac based on minimum lot size.

R-1(10000).description: Single-Family Residential district, 10,000 sq ft minimum lot subdistrict (Ch. 18.12). Standard single-family homes on larger lots. Max approx 4 du/ac.

R-1(8000).description: Single-Family Residential district, 8,000 sq ft minimum lot subdistrict (Ch. 18.12). Single-family homes. Max approx 5 du/ac.

R-1(7000).description: Single-Family Residential district, 7,000 sq ft minimum lot subdistrict (Ch. 18.12). Single-family homes. Max approx 6 du/ac.

R-1(6000).description: Single-Family Residential district, 6,000 sq ft minimum lot subdistrict (Ch. 18.12). Smallest standard single-family lots. Max approx 7 du/ac. New lots capped at 9,999 sq ft.

R-2.description: Low-Density Residential, Two-Family district (Ch. 18.10). Permits single-family and duplexes. Max approx 8 du/ac based on minimum lot area per unit.

RMD.description: Residential Mixed Density district (Ch. 18.10). Allows single-family, duplexes, and small multi-family. Transitional zone between single-family and multi-family areas. Max approx 12 du/ac.

RM-20.description: Multiple Family Residential, 20 du/ac district (Ch. 18.13). Formerly RM-15 (renamed and upzoned in 2022). Min lot size 8,500 sq ft. Allows apartments, condominiums, and townhouses. Max 20 du/ac.

RM-30.description: Multiple Family Residential, 30 du/ac district (Ch. 18.13). Medium-density multi-family residential. Min lot size 8,500 sq ft. Allows apartments, condominiums, and townhouses. Max 30 du/ac.

RM-40.description: Multiple Family Residential, 40 du/ac district (Ch. 18.13). High-density multi-family residential. Min lot size 8,500 sq ft. Allows apartments, condominiums, and townhouses. Max 40 du/ac.

CN.description: Neighborhood Commercial district (Ch. 18.16). Residential permitted on Housing Inventory Sites or as mixed-use. Max 15 du/ac on non-El Camino Real sites; up to 20 du/ac on Housing Inventory Sites per Housing Element. Standalone residential generally not permitted.

CC.description: Community Commercial district (Ch. 18.16). Residential permitted only on Housing Inventory Sites or as part of mixed-use per Housing Element. Max 15 du/ac where residential is allowed. Standalone residential generally prohibited.

CC(2).description: Community Commercial (2) district (Ch. 18.16). South El Camino Real area. Permits residential mixed-use at higher densities. Up to 40 du/ac on Housing Opportunity Sites. No minimum ground floor commercial FAR required for residential projects.

CS.description: Service Commercial district (Ch. 18.16). Residential permitted on Housing Inventory Sites, especially on El Camino Real corridor, as mixed-use. Up to 30 du/ac on Housing Opportunity Sites along El Camino Real. Standalone residential generally prohibited.

CD-C.description: Downtown Commercial - Commercial subdistrict (Ch. 18.18). Downtown core area. Residential allowed as mixed-use. Max 50 du/ac on Housing Opportunity Sites (transit-adjacent, highest density designation). Some sites subject to Comprehensive Plan density provisions.

CD-N.description: Downtown Commercial - Neighborhood subdistrict (Ch. 18.18). Downtown periphery/neighborhood transition area. Residential allowed as mixed-use. Max 40 du/ac on Housing Opportunity Sites.

CD-S.description: Downtown Commercial - South subdistrict (Ch. 18.18). South end of downtown. Residential allowed as mixed-use. Max approx 40 du/ac on designated sites.

MOR.description: Mature Office/Residential district (Ch. 18.20). Existing office uses with some residential retention. No new residential development generally permitted. Legacy single-family may remain.

ROLM.description: Research, Office, and Limited Manufacturing district (Ch. 18.20). Multi-family residential allowed by CUP, subject to RM-30 development standards (30 du/ac). On Housing Opportunity Sites, densities up to 50-90 du/ac may apply per Housing Element rezoning.

ROLM(E).description: Research, Office, and Limited Manufacturing (E) district (Ch. 18.20). Similar to ROLM. Multi-family residential allowed by CUP, subject to RM-30 standards. On Housing Opportunity Sites, higher densities may apply.

RP.description: Research Park district (Ch. 18.20). Intended for research, office, and light industrial uses. Residential not generally permitted. Stanford Research Park is the primary area under this designation.

RP(5).description: Research Park (5) district (Ch. 18.20). Subdistrict of RP with 5-acre minimum lot size. Residential not generally permitted.

GM.description: General Manufacturing district (Ch. 18.20). All residential development prohibited except on sites designated as Housing Element Opportunity Sites. On such sites, densities up to 50-90 du/ac are anticipated per Housing Element rezoning plans for areas along San Antonio Rd, W Bayshore Rd, and E Charleston Rd.

PC.description: Planned Community district (Ch. 18.38). Density is set by individual PC ordinance for each planned community. Requires at least 20% below-market-rate units. Density negotiated on a project-by-project basis; not subject to a single citywide standard.

PF.description: Public Facilities district (Ch. 18.28). Intended for public and quasi-public uses (schools, government buildings, utilities). Residential not generally permitted, though the city has evaluated allowing housing on PF-zoned parking lots designated as Housing Inventory Sites.

OS.description: Open Space district. Intended for parks, preserves, and recreation areas. No residential development permitted.

HIS-GM.description: Housing Inventory Sites in GM zone (per Sec. 18.14.020 and Housing Element). Sites along San Antonio Rd, W Bayshore Rd, E Charleston Rd rezoned to allow high-density residential. Min 20 du/ac (state law floor for recycled sites), max up to 90 du/ac.

HIS-ROLM.description: Housing Inventory Sites in ROLM zone (per Sec. 18.14.020 and Housing Element). Former office/manufacturing sites designated for housing. Min 20 du/ac, max up to 90 du/ac per Housing Element assumptions.
